scope: Third-pass stock screen moving one layer below commodity scarcity into logistics, storage, processing and treatment infrastructure. Research-only; scores are provisional research-priority scores and do not change Base Conviction.
coreRead: The most investable scarcity beneficiaries are increasingly companies that own difficult-to-replicate infrastructure between producer and end user: ammonia-capable ships and tanks, sulphuric-acid regeneration, industrial water-treatment systems, and complex refineries that can maximise middle-distillate output. Scarcity does not automatically benefit every upstream producer; the strongest signal is when rerouting, utilisation or realised margins are already improving.

newThemes.name: Ammonia Logistics: Rerouting + Storage Bottleneck
newThemes.status: New physical-infrastructure theme / fertilizer + energy crossover
newThemes.summary: The ammonia shortage is creating a logistics problem as well as a production problem. When Gulf supply is disrupted, replacement cargoes travel farther and require specialised refrigerated ships, terminals and storage. That can raise utilisation and transport economics even before new ammonia production capacity is built.
newThemes.whyDeveloping: Navigator Gas reported sharply higher Q2 TCE rates, fleet utilisation and EBITDA while explicitly noting that Asian consumers turned to North America for replacement LPG, ethane and ethylene volumes after Hormuz disruption constrained Middle Eastern supply. At the same time, Navigator is financing two new ammonia-capable carriers and Vopak already operates ammonia storage across Singapore, Malaysia, China and the US. The hidden bottleneck is therefore not only molecules of ammonia; it is the scarce infrastructure able to move and store them safely.

mainNews.title: Navigator Gas Q2 earnings jump as rerouted gas trade lifts rates and utilisation
mainNews.implication: Longer replacement routes are already converting geopolitical scarcity into higher ship utilisation and charter economics.

mainNews.title: Navigator finances two new ammonia-capable carriers
mainNews.implication: Specialised ammonia transport capacity is attracting fresh capital because the infrastructure itself is becoming strategically valuable.

mainNews.title: Vopak raises 2026 outlook as storage infrastructure remains highly utilised
mainNews.implication: High occupancy and growing gas/industrial infrastructure provide a lower-beta storage expression of increasingly complex commodity rerouting.

stockCandidates.thesis: Owns the world's largest handysize liquefied-gas carrier fleet, giving it direct exposure to longer replacement trade routes when Gulf molecules become unavailable. Unlike a speculative ammonia producer, the existing fleet is already monetising higher utilisation and freight economics.
evidence: Q2 net income attributable to shareholders rose to $53.0m from $21.5m a year earlier.
Q2 EBITDA increased to $101.6m from $71.9m.
Average fleet TCE rose to $33,946/day from $28,216/day YoY and $29,684/day in Q1.
Fleet utilisation increased to 90.8% from 84.2% YoY.
Management explicitly said Asian consumers shifted to North America for substitute LPG, ethane and ethylene volumes after Hormuz disruption.
Two 51,530 cbm ammonia-capable newbuilds are financed for 2028 delivery.
Early-August valuation was roughly 9-10x trailing earnings and near 1.1x book in public market snapshots.
risks: Shipping rates are cyclical and can reverse quickly if trade routes normalise.
Newbuild capital commitments increase execution and financing exposure.
The current earnings uplift is broader gas/petrochemical rerouting, not pure ammonia demand.
Fleet renewal and vessel sales can make reported earnings less comparable quarter to quarter.
stockCandidates.nextWork: Break out ammonia/LPG/petrochemical cargo exposure, charter coverage, vessel NAV and sensitivity of earnings to a 10-20% change in TCE rates.

stockCandidates.thesis: A lower-beta way to own commodity rerouting because specialised tanks, jetties and pipelines are difficult to reproduce. Vopak already handles ammonia in Singapore, Malaysia, China and the US while broader gas and industrial storage demand is supporting high occupancy and cash flow.
evidence: H1 proportional operating free cash flow reached EUR444m and 2026 FCF guidance was raised to around EUR820m.
2026 proportional EBITDA guidance was raised to EUR1.18-1.22bn.
Storage occupancy has remained around 91%.
EUR1.7bn of gas and industrial infrastructure growth commitments have been made, with EUR1.1bn under construction.
Vopak owns existing ammonia storage at Singapore Banyan and has ammonia handling/storage positions in Kertih, Caojing, Al-Jubail, Houston and Louisiana.
Early-August valuation was roughly 11x trailing and 13x forward earnings, with a roughly 4% dividend yield in public market snapshots.
risks: Ammonia is only one part of a diversified terminal portfolio, reducing thematic purity.
Large growth commitments require capital discipline and timely commissioning.
Chemical-storage demand remains weaker than gas/industrial storage.
Energy-transition terminal investments can take years to achieve full utilisation.
stockCandidates.nextWork: Map ammonia capacity by terminal, contract duration/occupancy economics and value the gas-industrial portfolio separately from oil/chemical terminals.

stockCandidates.theme: Industrial water treatment, reuse and process efficiency
stockCandidates.thesis: A specialist water-treatment platform exposed to semiconductor, industrial and municipal water efficiency. Q1 sales and core business profit grew despite a difficult cost environment, providing stronger current operating confirmation than several European water-chemical peers.
evidence: FY2027 Q1 net sales increased 14.3% YoY to JPY99.9bn.
Business profit increased 7.8% to JPY8.8bn.
Operating profit rose 58.5%, though reported profit also includes non-core effects and should not be extrapolated mechanically.
Full-year business-profit guidance is JPY61.5bn, up 7.2% on the comparable continuing-business base.
risks: The share price has rerated sharply and valuation is no longer obviously cheap.
Headline operating-profit growth is stronger than underlying business-profit growth because of non-core effects.
Semiconductor and industrial customers remain cyclical.
stockCandidates.nextWork: Split Electronics versus General Industry growth, service/chemical recurring revenue, semiconductor exposure and normalised valuation after non-core gains.

stockCandidates.theme: High refinery utilisation with upstream optionality
stockCandidates.thesis: Cenovus is less pure than VLO/MPC/PSX but offers an unusual two-sided structure: upstream benefits from crude strength while its refineries capture elevated product cracks. That reduces dependence on correctly timing whether the shortage remains in crude or migrates deeper into products.
evidence: Q2 free funds flow reached C$3.8bn and net earnings C$2.87bn.
Downstream crude utilisation was 95% overall and 96% in US refining.
Downstream operating margin increased to C$953m from C$734m QoQ as crack spreads strengthened.
Net debt fell materially during the quarter while C$1.4bn was returned to shareholders.
risks: Less pure exposure to diesel cracks than independent refiners.
Oil-sands and crude-price beta can dominate refinery economics.
Planned Q3-Q4 US refining maintenance will temporarily reduce throughput.
stockCandidates.nextWork: Quantify product-yield mix, refining market capture and valuation versus VLO/MPC/PSX after the large sector rerating.

stockCandidates.thesis: Q2 confirms very strong capture of the product shortage, but the stock has already rerated to recent highs. The proposed lubricants separation adds a corporate catalyst but makes the near-term thesis less purely about diesel scarcity.
evidence: Q2 net income reached $892m, the highest quarterly profit since 2022.
Adjusted refinery gross margin per barrel rose 57.3% to $25.95.
Refining adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to about $1.02bn.
Quarterly dividend was raised 5%.
risks: Shares were near a 52-week high by Aug. 20 after a major sector rerating.
Diesel/gasoline cracks can mean-revert rapidly.
Lubricants spin-off adds execution and sum-of-the-parts uncertainty.
stockCandidates.nextWork: Compare refinery complexity, distillate yield and valuation with VLO/MPC/PSX; wait for a better technical entry unless cracks re-accelerate.

stockCandidates.thesis: The margin leverage is enormous when cracks widen, but operational risk and balance-sheet cyclicality make it a much less forgiving expression than VLO/MPC/PSX.
evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached about $1.24bn versus roughly $70m a year earlier.
Gross refining margin reached $23.40/bbl versus $8.38/bbl a year earlier.
The company has broad US coastal refinery exposure that can benefit from export-driven product scarcity.
risks: Martinez refinery fire costs and insurance effects complicate reported results.
Higher operating costs and concentrated refinery-event risk.
Much higher earnings volatility than the larger refiners.
stockCandidates.nextWork: Normalise earnings excluding insurance/fire effects and compare net debt, maintenance schedule and distillate yield with larger refiners.

falseFriends.reason: Water Solutions revenue grew, but Q2 group operative EBITDA fell 15% and Water Solutions margin dropped to 17.4% from 22.9% as Iran-war raw-material and logistics inflation overwhelmed pricing. Strong structural water theme, weak current scarcity capture.

researchConclusion: NVGS is the strongest genuinely new stock from the deep-bottleneck pass because trade rerouting is already visible in both utilisation and charter economics at a still-moderate valuation. Vopak is the cleaner lower-beta infrastructure counterpart. Kurita improves the industrial-water bench but is not as cheap as MWA. In refining, CVE adds a useful integrated hedge while DINO and PBF are tactical secondary candidates behind VLO/MPC/PSX.
